newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Peters says won't intervene in NZ dollar.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Peters says won't intervene in NZ dollar.

text.p: New Zealand Treasurer Winston Peters told reporters on Tuesday the government had a policy of not intervening in the New Zealand dollar for any perceived short term crisis.
In answer to questions, Peters said: "You've got a very clear steer today that we're not going to take precipitative action and to react to the mentality of crisis.
"In fact, the best thing that we can do is to observe...the market itself is a clear commentator on what the levels should be."
Peters said he was not surprised there were no questions about the level of the New Zealand dollar at a business meeting he had just attended.
He said the business briefing got a very clear indication there would be no short term solutions to the high currency.
Farmers who were looking for a short term palliative would be comforted that the government was looking at other efficiencies which would be exacted from the economy to assist them.

Asked whether the level of the New Zealand dollar reflected a strong economy, Peters said he had received a very strong message from a farming leader at the breakfast meeting that farmers saw intervention in the currency as counter-productive.
"Presumably he speaks on behalf of the farming community," Peters said.

"His message was very, very plain; he did not want to see me interfere with it (the Kiwi) and he got an assurance that I will not interfere in the interests of reacting to some sort of perceived short term crisis."
